purpose: Apraclonidine is an eye drop used to lower pressure inside the eye. It is commonly used before and after certain laser eye procedures to prevent a dangerous spike in eye pressure. It may also be used short-term in people with glaucoma when other medications are not controlling their eye pressure well enough.
how_it_works: Your eye constantly makes a fluid called aqueous humor, and if too much builds up, it raises the pressure inside your eye. Apraclonidine works by telling the eye to produce less of this fluid and may also help it drain a little better. This lowers the pressure, which helps protect the optic nerve and your vision.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include eye redness, itching, burning, or discomfort after putting in the drops. You may also notice your upper eyelid lifting slightly or your pupil getting smaller. Some people feel a dry mouth or nose, headache, or drowsiness. These are usually mild and temporary.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you take any blood pressure medicines, antidepressants (especially MAO inhibitors), or heart medications, as serious interactions can occur. Do not use this medication if you are allergic to clonidine. It is not recommended for long-term use because many patients develop an allergic reaction over time, causing increased redness and swelling. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you, as it can cause drowsiness.
typical_dosing: For laser eye procedures, one drop is usually placed in the affected eye about one hour before the procedure and another drop right after. For short-term glaucoma management, the usual dose is one drop in the affected eye three times a day. Always follow your eye doctor's exact instructions.
